To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ROCK-mediated selective activation of the unfolded protein response pathway in the epithelial compartment of breast cancer drives the recruitment of cancer-associated fibrobasts, which are part of tumour microenvironment, and promotes tumour growth through a CRELD-dependent mechanism.

Rho-associated kinases (ROCKs) in the mamary tumour epithelilium selectively actuate protein-kinase R-like endoplasmatic reticulum kinase to recruit and educate cancer-associated fibroblast (CAFs), part of the cancerous microenviroment, via the paracrine cysteine-rich protein CRELD2.

Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK), which is expressed in the mammary epithelial cells of breast tumours, selectively activates PERK, causing the recruitment and education of tumour promoting cancer-associated fibroblast (CAFs) through a cysteine-rich protein called CRELD2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that drive cancer progression.
the molecular mechanisms that control the development of cancer and the progression of tumours, and how tumour cells interact with the microenvironment to promote tumour growth.
understanding the molecular basis of cancer-associated fibrosis and the role of cancer-associated fibrotic microenvironment in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ROCK–PERK signalling axis promotes the recruitment and function of CAFs in the breast cancer microenvironment through the paracrine CRELD2 factor, and thus contributes to tumour growth.
ROCK upregulation in breast cancer epithelial cells promotes tumourigenesis through CRELD2-dependent recruitment and function of CAFs.
the study shows a novel mechanism of how ROCK-mediated selective activation of the PERK signalling pathway in the tumour epithelum causes fibroblast reporgramming and tumour progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ROCK upregulation in the epithelial compartment leads to selective activation of PERKI signalling and the recruitment and education of CAFs through CRELD2, which is a paracrine factor.
ROCK selectively activates the PERK pathway in epithelial cells, which leads to the recruitment of CAFs through the CRELD2 pathway.
the ROCK-mediated selective activation of the PERK signalling pathway causes fibroblast education and tumour progression in the mammary gland through a CRELD protein-dependent mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ROCK–PERK pathway is a key regulator of the cancer micro-environment, with therapeutic potential.
